column1: # Behaviour-label vocabulary: the levels below constructs.txt (ADR 0008; PROTOCOL.md section 14).
# constructs.txt is the top level and is not repeated here. Every line below is a child label, written
# "Parent > child" with the parent's text verbatim; a child's parent is a top-level label or an earlier line of this file.
# A word carries a child label by listing the whole text in its `exercises`, exactly as it lists a top-level label.
# Columns, separated by tabs:
#   label            Parent > child (children of children chain: A > b > c)
#   checked_against  the existing labels this one was compared with before it was admitted, separated by ";": its
#                    parent first, then its siblings and the other labels it could be confused with. This is
#                    the admission record: a label is admitted only when it names something none of those does.
#   meaning          one line: the behaviour or interaction it names
# `python3 scripts/suite.py check` fails on a label that is in neither constructs.txt nor here, a line whose parent
# or checked label does not exist, and a line no word carries.
